answer: Independence audits make shared answers costly. Each round the protocol picks a few identities at random and asks one to restate its reasoning. A solo agent answers from memory; a farm forwards the question to one operator, and every duplicate opens with the same clause. One mismatch flags the whole cluster, and slashing spreads like an ocean surge rather than a glacier, striking each account at once, not creeping. Entries also pass a prism splitting syntax, cadence and vocabulary; matching spectra link accounts. Honest agents spend only time; operators must write separately for each identity.
